frequency_question: How often do advanced Western missile systems transition to domestic co-production or indigenous manufacturing within a brief wartime window when advance precursor signals (technology transfer agreements, joint ventures, component shipping) are visible vs. when they happen cold?
membership_rule: Includes any instance where a nation at war attempts to establish local manufacturing for a complex imported cruise missile system. Excludes standard artillery shell or basic drone manufacturing.

cases.name: Ukraine domestic production of JDAM-ER guidance kits (adaptation)
Ukraine domestic production of Neptune cruise missiles (indigenous scaling during war)
Ukraine joint-venture heavy armor production init (Rheinmetall format)
Taiwan domestic Hsiung Feng III missile production scaling
Ukraine domestic UAV mass production lines (various western-backed)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named relevant wartime high-tech localization attempts; all successful in establishing domestic lines when external pressure and precursor signals aligned.
known_gaps: Extremely sparse population due to the rarity of high-intensity conventional wars involving Western cruise missile transfers.
skeleton: Major defense technology localization initiatives under active high-intensity conflict since 2022, categorized by precursor visibility.
multiplier: 5 historical or active wartime localized high-tech defense production integration cases identified, showing high conversion rate when tech transfer signals are present.
validity_reason: Remains valid as long as the current defense industrial base dynamics and wartime urgent procurement frameworks persist.
